verdict.rationale: BugSnag documents stability as the share of error-free sessions, with configurable stability targets, plus release filtering, release annotations on the timeline, and a 'does not equal' release filter that enables rough cross-release comparison. However, the evidence never mentions crash-free users, adoption per release, or a dedicated canary-vs-stable comparison view. Missing for 10: crash-free users metric, per-release adoption tracking, explicit side-by-side canary vs last-stable release comparison, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can watch release health — crash-free sessions and users, adoption per release — and compare a canary release against the last stable one

citations.quote: Stability is a measure of the proportion of user application sessions that are error free.
Monitor the stability of your application and measure progress against stability targets.
filter your dashboard by release and identify which release errors were introduced in.
see release annotations on the timeline to correlate new versions with changes in error rates.
Adding a "does not equal" operator for release in the shared Release filter
